When we started this campaign in my campaign manager's garage, building a lectern because we didn't have one for launch day, this wasn't a sure thing. Nothing about this was a given. But working people showed up, kept showing up, and now the national party knows what we have known for a long time. **We can win this race.** Red to Blue means resources, infrastructure, and support we didn't have before. It also means the target on our back just got bigger. We're going to need to be ready for what comes next. Max Miller loaned himself $1 million to try to save his campaign after both of Ohio's Republican Senators called for him to leave the race. His family called him unfit to serve. He's going to call every lobbyist and corporate favor he has to try to win this race. Meanwhile, I've spent my whole life in this district, around people who work hard and wonder if anyone in Washington actually understands their lives. I do. Because I've lived them. That's what I'm bringing to Congress, and that's what this campaign has been about from day one. [**We're not done yet. The road to taking back the House goes through Ohio. subject: If you care about America, read this first
body:
We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.
_Please see a special message from our sponsor. If you would like to unsubscribe, visit this[link](http://links.conservative-today.com/s/u/3PRKpgEn5Xja0nRz1uDokWdjf5UaOiYtKZmPDCtqrHgiAEky90tDdtTXlf1qC592LZOKdX6LQWp74X-l1RUuOg933A4zjUPgsGjvL8dx1GPQt-Seztqei6r03en3mZ1SBuFSVWn01wJgFep5fti7zjxNKEQSxPOXB-Pgk15BK9mw3FPNvUYvR11n/3MPOzH0d4TLD6BxCFAHcSsLCLTD_4p7W/23)_
| | |
---
| | Friend,
---
I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

Less than a year later...

**We 're in 3,300 schools. **

**Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. **

**Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. **

_That shouldn 't be possible. _

Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day.

And yet... it's still happening.

_But friend, here 's the part you need to understand: _

This is not a victory. It's a foothold.

_Because in the other 87% of schools? _

There is no resistance. None.

Just one-sided propaganda from the Left.

One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them.

That's the reality.

The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are.

The question is whether it's enough.

Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America...

They're not the majority. _They 're the exception. _

They're the ones willing to take the heat.

The ones willing to stand alone.

The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: _" I love this country." _

We have a choice.

Back them. _Or leave them on their own. _

**Because when a student starts a chapter, we send them an activism kit -- with American flags. Pocket Constitutions. Leadership tools. **

Everything they need to actually stand their ground.

Not symbolically. For real.

They've already made the decision to lead.

All they're waiting on... is you and me.

**Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. **

I want to talk to the outdoor industry. To the brands, the resorts, the hotels, the restaurants, the whole outdoor and snow economy.
You have been quiet.
You have been quiet while people get pulled off the street by masked agents who will not show a badge or a warrant. You have been quiet while tens of thousands of people sit in detention centers, most of them are Black and brown, and most of them have never been charged with a crime.
Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..OGw_CRaliNsG2dF8ij2Ubf3GnTh7Tabq-LTZaP6PO5c?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=211216905)
You have been quiet while this administration moves to strip protections from more than [86 million acres of public land](https://substack.com/redirect/d9a30134-3f14-4376-8a68-b7593c1837d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That is not an Utah problem. That is the Boundary Waters. That is Alaska. That is the forests your customers drive to every weekend. Three million of those acres are the two Utah monuments now open to mining claims, while bulldozers plow through a national park.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ade33929-bb47-49f7-b6a1-1d89af411844?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Valley of the gods, one of many areas cut from Bears Ears National Monument.
Your industry runs on immigrant labor. Every one of you knows this. The J-1 students who run the lifts and the rental shops. The H-2B workers who clean the rooms, cook the food, and keep the whole operation moving all season long. You cannot open your doors without them. You built your business model around them. And now you will not say their names.
I am tired of watching an entire industry decide that saying nothing is a strategy. Do not tell me this industry does not do politics. In 2017 you pulled Outdoor Retailer out of Salt Lake City over Bears Ears. You knew exactly how to use your power then. Nothing about the last nine years made you weaker. It made you quieter.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/53897a6a-09e6-4134-93dd-339e08a0d6c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Protesting at the Outdoor Retailer trade show in 2017 when the industry decided to leave Utah over the decision to undo protections for Bears Ears.
The best time to speak up was before this monster got elected. The next best time is right now.
I am not asking you to do something I have not done. I have lost partnerships for saying this out loud. I ran for the U.S. Senate to try to stop us from getting here. I know exactly what it costs.
I am telling you it costs less than you think, and a lot less than what we lose if we all keep quiet.
And let's be honest about what this has cost you. The tariffs raised the price of every piece of gear you sell and every piece you make overseas. The crisis around the Strait of Hormuz has driven up fuel and shipping costs, which means everything on your shelves costs more to get there. Trips are getting canceled. People are holding onto their money. And the attacks on public lands and the refusal to do anything about climate change are coming straight for the snow and outdoors you sell.
You are hurting. Your margins are hurting. Your season is hurting.
What did the quiet get you? Tariffs anyway. Shipping costs anyway. Your public lands opened to mining anyway. You bought nothing.
Your industry is being decimated by the same administration you are afraid to name. You have every reason in the world to use your voice and every lever of power you have.
This is not a policy disagreement. If they can do this to immigrants without due process, there is nothing stopping them from doing it to anyone. You are next. Your employees are next. Your customers are next.
I know what you are afraid of. You are afraid of being targeted by this administration. But you are complying in advance, which is far more dangerous. You are afraid of alienating customers. But I'd argue that Neo-Nazis and white supremacists should be alienated. If someone stops buying your skis because you said people deserve due process, that is not a customer you needed. And every day you stay silent to protect that sale, you are telling the rest of us exactly what your values are worth.
So here is the one thing I am asking you to do. Register your customers to vote.
You have millions of people walking through your doors, standing in your lift lines, and opening your emails. Put voter registration in your stores. Run drives at your base areas and your trailhead events. Put a link in every newsletter you send. Give your employees paid time to vote. None of this is partisan and none of it is risky. It is the single most powerful thing a company your size can do, and it is sitting right there.
If you do not want to say anything about immigration or public lands, fine. Register your customers to vote and let them handle it. That is how we vote these assholes out.
You have marketing budgets. You have millions of followers. You have lobbyists in Washington. We are a trillion dollar industry. Let's start acting like it.
All of this comes from a kid who got her start as a green vest cashier at REI. A kid who snuck into her first Outdoor Retailer on a borrowed badge because she wanted in so badly. I grew up in this industry. I have made my living in it. I love these mountains and I love these companies and this gear and these customers with my whole heart.
That is why I am asking. I am not trying to burn this down. I am trying to make sure there is something left of it.
Find your moral courage. Find your backbone.
In other news:
Bulldozers started clearing land inside Big Bend National Park in Texas. The contract is worth 1.7 billion dollars and covers roughly 200 miles of patrol roads and 17 miles of barriers through one of the wildest places left in this country. Half a million people visit Big Bend every year.
Santa Elena Canyon is already fifteen hundred feet of wall. It has been working fine for millions of years.
You do not fix immigration by bulldozing a national park. If you want to tell your members of Congress that, I [made it take about ninety seconds](https://substack.com/redirect/66a85069-5061-4790-b45b-1f073e04728d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
I got back from the Western Arctic, where I spent 8 days paddling 70 miles to see new oil wells drilled last winter by ConocoPhillips that were approved by Trump in a special area that should be protected. I keep thinking about 60,000 caribou that are born there and the Inupiat people who depend on the caribou for subsistence.

Fellow Patriot,

**I want to read you something Chuck Schumer said.**

_"Democrats support voter ID. In fact, we included it, and it is included, in our Freedom to Vote legislation several years ago."_

****Those are his exact words.** **

Schumer led every single Senate Democrat to vote against it. The same day he said Democrats support it.

subject: It's not just Paxton vs. Talarico

body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241014%2E444211%2EDno9CD)
While the marquee races for senate and governor understandably get the lion’s share of attention and dollars, there are hundreds of other elections in Texas that are critically important.
Called “down ballot” races, these contests for congress, state legislature and county government will decide the balance of power in Texas and in America.
Let me quickly explain.
While James Talarico will raise the money and press attention befitting a top-tier candidate for senate, he will not by himself be able to beat Ken Paxton. It’s not because of any shortcoming on his part — I don’t know that Texas Democrats have produced as talented a candidate in decades — instead, it’s because James is up against the combined spending of the entire Republican-billionaire complex and 30+ years of entrenched GOP power in Texas.
To overcome that he needs leaders on the frontlines who can meet and turn out voters where they are in every one of the 254 counties of Texas. That’s why Powered by People worked so hard to recruit a Democrat to run in every Congressional and state legislative race, something that hasn’t happened in 50 years! That's 150 state house candidates, 16 state senate candidates and 38 congressional candidates. We’re also supporting candidates for county commissioner and county judge, elevating those who will bring in new and lapsed voters for their local races and for the top-of-the-ticket showdown as well.
I know from experience how powerful this can be. When I ran for Senate in 2018, we had amazing first time front line candidates — like James Talarico in his first bid for State Rep — who not only won their races but brought in the local voters who helped me get within 2.6% of beating Ted Cruz. Working together we won 12 seats in the state house, 2 in Congress and 19 judicial positions in Harris County alone.
That’s why Powered by People works with local candidates at all places of the ballot and why from time to time I’ll ask you to support these front line candidates.
Their success is critical to winning Texas and to making James the 51st vote in the Senate.
[**Please pitch in right now to help us organize, register, and mobilize voters across Texas — so we can elect the leaders Texas deserves.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260814.cF00BT&refcode=ema20260814-241014&t=3&akid=241014%2E444211%2EDno9CD)

Thank you,
Beto

**A federal judge just blocked President Trump’s latest attempt to use the Postal Service to interfere with vote-by-mail.** _That is a big deal for Oregon._ Trump’s plan would have turned the Postal Service into something it was never meant to be: a gatekeeper for who gets to vote by mail. In Oregon, we know better. The Postal Service delivers ballots. Oregonians decide elections. And this week, the court agreed that Trump cannot simply shove his way into state elections because he does not like how people vote. **But I want to be clear: this is one victory in a much longer fight.** President Trump and his allies are not going to stop trying to undermine vote-by-mail. They are not going to stop spreading lies about our elections. And they are not going to stop looking for new ways to make voting harder, more confusing, and less accessible. _So we cannot stop either._ As Oregon’s Secretary of State, I will keep defending our vote-by-mail system, protecting every eligible voter, and fighting back every time Washington tries to interfere with Oregon elections. We have beaten them in court before. We are prepared to do it again. And again. And again. Federal vaccine rules just changed. Colorado’s school requirements didn’t.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey friends,
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** New sports betting rules (SB26-131) took effect Aug. 12, [banning credit card deposits](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and capping daily online deposits at six. The Colorado NRA is [suing to block SB25-003's new mandatory safety training](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for buying certain semiautomatic firearms. Colorado added 28,600 jobs in June [despite economic headwinds](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Six [new traffic laws took effect](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), including Magnus's Law on breathalyzer offers after serious crashes. [Youth vendor markets](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for kids 5-17 hit Centennial (Aug. 14) and Castle Rock (Aug. 22). And [Colorado's school vaccine requirements stay unchanged](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) under SB26-032, despite Trump's new federal "Gold Standard" schedule scaling back routine childhood vaccines.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** Karoline Leavitt is [stepping down as White House press secretary](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) at month's end to focus on her two young children, calling the role "the honor and adventure of a lifetime." Trump says she'll stay on as a top outside advisor and GOP voice.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Greg Walcher argued the Forest Service's planned overhaul is overdue, citing a [75% drop in professional foresters](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) since 1989. Cory Gaines [flagged a rare judicial split](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.): the state commission called 13th District Judge Dina Christiansen fit for office while still urging an improvement plan, even as local evaluators recommended against retaining her; two other judges also drew do-not-retain marks.
This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, August 14, 2026.
– Team RMV

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Federal vaccine rules just changed. Colorado’s school requirements didn’t.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY RMV STAFF, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
When President Donald Trump signed an executive order establishing a new federal “Gold Standard” childhood vaccine schedule this week, it marked a major shift in federal vaccine recommendations.
The administration’s new framework reduces the number of diseases for which vaccines are routinely recommended for all children, moves several vaccines into high-risk or shared clinical decision-making categories, and encourages greater parental involvement in vaccination decisions.
But for Colorado families, the announcement raised an immediate question: If the federal government has changed its recommendations, why haven’t Colorado’s school vaccine requirements changed?
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Kids run the booths at two Front Range markets this month](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_Free enterprise gets a hands-on lesson as Colorado kids build real businesses, set real prices, and pocket real profits at two Front Range markets this month._
* **Real business, real ownership:** Kids Markets, running events Aug. 14 in Centennial and Aug. 22 in Castle Rock for vendors ages 5-17, lets kids handle everything themselves — pricing, inventory, sales, and counting earnings — while adults only manage the venue and logistics.
* **Rooted in a fight for economic freedom:** The program traces back to Utah's 2017 "Lemonade Stand Law," pushed by Libertas Utah after kids were shut down for selling without permits, and has since grown to markets in 26 states under Connor Boyack's Libertas Network, which openly frames the events as introducing families to free-market principles through experience rather than lectures.
* **Skills that stick, with a growing Colorado footprint:** Beyond the two August dates, Kids Markets has additional Front Range events through September in Colorado Springs, Southglenn, Fountain, Thornton, and Parker, giving young entrepreneurs firsthand lessons in pricing, marketing, and customer service that no classroom can replicate.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

**[Weiser’s Blueprint: More offices, in the name of streamlining](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | AUGUST 12** _Phil Weiser’s plan for Colorado runs 109 pages. It promises, throughout the document, to make state government simpler, faster, and less tangled in its own rules. It also proposes a new set of offices, officers, and coordinating teams to carry it out._
**[Colorado law already protects Douglas County teachers. Why a union contract?](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY MARTHA CARVER | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 12** _You may be aware that the Douglas County Federation (DCF), the teachers’ union, is asking the Douglas County School District to engage in Collective Bargaining. Before making a major shift in school governance, district leaders should recognize the protections already in place and require clear support from a majority of teachers._

**[Denver ballot measure would drop citizenship rule for police-fire oversight board](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY SHAINA COLE | LOCAL | AUGUST 11**
****_This November, Denver voters will decide whether to change the city charter with a ballot question that never mentions the word “citizenship.” The question they’ll see asks whether the charter should be “amended to modernize the Civil Service Commission and Department of Safety by removing outdated language, giving City Council the ability to add duties via code, and providing for an extension of probation when required for medical, military, or other approved leave.”_

name: Justice Democrats
subject: More than $100 million
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Since AIPAC first created its super PAC in 2022, it “has spent more money
on TV, radio, and digital ads in federal elections over the past three
election cycles than any other special interest group not linked to a
political party,” according to the New York Times.

Now, AIPAC and United Democracy Project are on track to spend more this
cycle than ever before, dropping $104.3 million on the 2026 midterm
elections — and we’re still 3 months out from the general election.

Per Sludge, it’s the second election cycle in a row that this pro-Israel
lobby group has spent over $100 million to influence races and buy seats
in the halls of power.

The vast majority of their 2026 primary spending was against progressive,
pro-peace candidates in Democratic primaries, including multiple Justice
Democrats. It was their most expensive primary season yet:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260814.OmeTj4&refcode=em20260814-38164&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=38164%2E1203867%2EAeUX7x ]Bar graph showing AIPAC spending in primaries by party, with blue
representing Democratic and red representing Republican. 2022: $27.2
million Democratic; 2024: $40.3 million Democratic, $3.08 million
Republican; 2026: $63 million Democratic, $4.16 million Republican

In MO-01, they spent $3 million to save Wesley Bell’s seat against Cori
Bush, who they previously bought a seat for in 2024. They spent over $4
million in the IL-09 primary, where Justice Democrat Kat Abughazaleh lost
— but so did AIPAC’s pick. And in IL-08, they dropped $4.6 million to
defeat JD candidate Junaid Ahmed.

But they and their donors also spent millions against Justice Democrats
like Darializa Avila Chevalier, Claire Valdez, Chris Rabb, Melat Kiros,
Donavan McKinney, Dr. Adam Hamawy, and Justin J. Pearson and LOST.

With a supermajority of Democratic voters opposed to the Israeli
government’s genocide in Gaza and war crimes elsewhere, and tired of their
tax dollars going to fund it, AIPAC is now having to spend more to win
races, all while rarely mentioning the issue of “Israel” in their ads.
Their brand is increasingly toxic, and their results are mixed.

It goes to show that our push to reject AIPAC in the Democratic Party is
working — it’s only become harder and more expensive for their network to
win elections.

But our fight to end their control of Congress isn’t over. In fact, we
already know they’re bundling donations for Justin J. Pearson’s far-right
opponent in the race for TN-09 and AIPAC’s repeatedly backed Angela
Gonzales-Torres and Mai Vang’s incumbent opponents in California.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260814.OmeTj4&refcode=em20260814-38164&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=38164%2E1203867%2EAeUX7x ]Help Justice Democrats keep up the fight against AIPAC: chip in

In solidarity,

# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=688%2E127862%2EVE8Jbl)
Nevada’s governor’s race is anyone’s game to win right now.
A recent poll shows we are TIED with MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo, 45 to 45.
Being in a tied race means every single action we take from this moment on matters. **There's no such thing as a spectator right now.**

My story is Wisconsin’s story. I was born and raised in Milwaukee in a union household. My father was a master electrician and my mother worked in the service industry. Just like so many families in Wisconsin, they worked hard. But also like many families, they struggled with addiction and mental health issues.
Growing up, I watched my family fight every single day just to get by. I learned that when systems fail, families pay the price. **But I also learned that grit, resilience, and hope for a better tomorrow can carry us through even the toughest challenges.**
To me, these challenges aren’t just policy issues. They’re lived experiences. My wife, Ericka, and I are raising three daughters in Milwaukee, which keeps me focused on what policy really means at the kitchen table, not just in Madison.
As Milwaukee County Executive and as a State Assemblyman before that, I’ve also seen first-hand how good government can actually improve people’s lives. I believe that when we commit to putting working families first and bringing the basics back within reach, we create communities where every Wisconsinite can thrive. **Derek, I promise you that’s not just a nice campaign slogan – it’s how I govern.**
But if you’ll forgive a little more campaign talk, the same can’t be said for Tom Tiffany.
Tiffany cares about making Wisconsin better for billionaires like Elon Musk and the Uihlein family, _NOT_ for everyday folks like you and me.
Tiffany’s priority is advancing Trump’s MAGA agenda in our state, _NOT_ creating good government that lifts people up and helps them thrive.

Now, let’s get to know each other. | | | | My name is David Crowley, and I am so proud to introduce myself as your official Democratic nominee for Governor of Wisconsin! I want to take a moment to tell you why I’m in this race. But first, I need to cut right to the chase: Wisconsin can’t afford four years of Tom Tiffany in the Governor’s office. Wisconsinites deserve leaders who will put working people over billionaires and fight for Wisconsin’s future – not Trump’s MAGA agenda. We have just 81 days to win this thing, Derek, so I need you with me now. | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process immediately: | | | | | | Alright, that’s enough campaign talk. Let’s get to know each other, Derek. My story is Wisconsin’s story. I was born and raised in Milwaukee in a union household. My father was a master electrician and my mother worked in the service industry. Just like so many families in Wisconsin, they worked hard. But also like many families, they struggled with addiction and mental health issues. Growing up, I watched my family fight every single day just to get by. I learned that when systems fail, families pay the price. But I also learned that grit, resilience, and hope for a better tomorrow can carry us through even the toughest challenges. To me, these challenges aren’t just policy issues. They’re lived experiences. My wife, Ericka, and I are raising three daughters in Milwaukee, which keeps me focused on what policy really means at the kitchen table, not just in Madison. As Milwaukee County Executive and as a State Assemblyman before that, I’ve also seen first-hand how good government can actually improve people’s lives. I believe that when we commit to putting working families first and bringing the basics back within reach, we create communities where every Wisconsinite can thrive. Derek, I promise you that’s not just a nice campaign slogan – it’s how I govern. But if you’ll forgive a little more campaign talk, the same can’t be said for Tom Tiffany. Tiffany cares about making Wisconsin better for billionaires like Elon Musk and the Uihlein family, NOT for everyday folks like you and me. Tiffany’s priority is advancing Trump’s MAGA agenda in our state, NOT creating good government that lifts people up and helps them thrive. Hi, it's Quentin James, Founder and President of The Collective PAC. Paul Rivera is a friend and one of the most experienced operatives in Democratic politics. When the [DNC commissioned him to conduct the party's post-2024 review](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e4975af3-be64-4fc5-bf7a-d1a5694bde07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), he did what serious people do: he interviewed operatives in all 50 states, dug into precinct-level data, and wrote down what he found, whether or not it was comfortable.
And what did the DNC do with it? They shelved it. For months. It took pressure from state parties, governors, and donors, plus CNN preparing to publish a leaked copy, before the committee finally posted the draft online. And even then, they released it covered in red-ink annotations distancing themselves from their own commissioned report, with entire sections missing. The chair later apologized, admitting that trying to avoid a distraction created a bigger one.
Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9jb2xsZWN0aXZlcGFjLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MjExMjE5OTg5LCJzIjo2ODIwNjM3LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzg2NzM0OTU1LCJleHAiOjIxMDIzMTA5NTUsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.Q6RI-rdFgokb6BaXUvfACWws0COqONfOZrkG8JDmk-g?)
Let me be plain: that was a disaster. Not because of the leaks or the process drama, but because of what it signaled. The party sat on a document containing the clearest data we have on the erosion of Black voter participation, during the exact window when that data should have been driving 2026 planning. You cannot say Black voters are the base of this party and then bury the report that shows the base cracking.
So let's do what the DNC wouldn't. Let's take the findings seriously.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ea6e693d-54e6-4ceb-a36e-b31d957c2e90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

## What the report actually says about the Black vote
The numbers are stark. Of the 792 counties and jurisdictions in America with a Black population of ten percent or more, 658 shifted toward Trump in 2024. Only 134 moved our way.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/065d73dc-3c5d-4aaf-94da-6751af02b9ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Black turnout dropped 9.6 points nationally from 2020. Among Black voters 18 to 24, it fell 13 points. Among those 25 to 34, nearly 15 points. Every one of the top 15 counties by Black population moved toward Trump, with Black turnout collapsing by 12 points or more in Cook County, Harris County, Dallas, Broward, and Shelby. Mississippi, the Blackest state in the nation, saw Harris lose ground in all but one county.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8128db00-901c-472e-82d2-6aaf683048ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Here is the part everyone needs to sit with: this was not mass conversion to the Republican Party. It was turnout collapse. Millions of Black voters who showed up in 2020 stayed home in 2024. And the pattern tells you why. In the battleground states where real money and real organizing landed, the drops were far smaller. Fulton County fell just 2.5 points. Wayne County, 4. Philadelphia held better than Chicago or Houston. Investment worked. Disinvestment failed. Rivera calls it what it is: a near-generational lack of investment in Black communities, especially across the South and the Black Belt, finally coming due.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/67f5fb30-2801-4803-9caa-f8f2f653b65e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And here is the number that puts the whole thing in context. As Ashley Etienne, who ran communications for Vice President Harris and Speaker Pelosi, [has reported from her own analysis of the autopsy: the Democratic ecosystem spent roughly $8 billion in 2024, and approximately 1 percent of it was invested in Black voters.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/9eb216ce-821f-49b8-9d7a-fc8d577e111f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) One percent. For the most loyal voting bloc in American politics. Ashley laid it out in her Essence op-ed, "The Party We Built, The Bill Has Come Due," and she is right. Black voters delivered victory after victory, and the returns have not been mutual. Read the turnout table above and then read that 1 percent figure again. These are not two separate stories. They are cause and effect.
The report also flags a warning light for the future. Younger Black voters are registering as Democrats at far lower rates than their parents and grandparents. By 2028, millions of Black voters under 34 will have never had the chance to cast a ballot for Barack Obama. The connection is not inherited. It has to be earned, and right now nobody at the national level is earning it.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/647503cb-9d5d-4e99-82e1-9de9cde59ba1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The good news is in there too. Virginia 2025 proved the fix works. A real coordinated campaign, grounded in voter research and focused on re-engaging Black voters across the Commonwealth, delivered Abigail Spanberger 93 percent of the Black vote, better than Harris, better than Biden, better than McAuliffe. This is not a mystery. It is a choice.
## We've been proving this thesis for ten years
At The Collective PAC, this is not a new conversation for us. We were founded on the premise the report finally puts in writing: Black political power does not maintain itself. It has to be built, funded, and defended, cycle after cycle, in the years between elections and not just the ninety days before one. Over the past decade we have helped elect Black leaders up and down the ballot, trained roughly 2,000 operatives, and moved more than $50 million into Black candidates and Black political infrastructure, much of it in the exact states and counties Rivera's maps show bleeding out.
So when the report says investment works and disinvestment fails, we do not read that as analysis. We read it as our operating history. Georgia and North Carolina held better than the rest of the South because people built infrastructure there. The question for the party is whether it will finally fund that model everywhere, or keep treating Black turnout as a renewable resource that regenerates on its own. It does not. The data now proves it.
## 80 days. Here's the assignment.
Early voting starts in weeks in some states. National Early Vote Day is October 24. There is no time for another listening tour. Here is what each layer of this ecosystem must do right now.
**The DNC** must convert its own report from a public relations problem into an operating plan. Fund the When We Count registration pilot at scale in Black communities, starting with the under-registered turf in the newly gerrymandered districts Republicans just drew. Accelerate the county chair recruitment project in the Black Belt, where hundreds of majority-Black counties have gone cycle after cycle with no organized party presence. And put resources, not statements, behind the state parties carrying Senate and governor races.
**The party committees** (DSCC, DCCC, DGA, DLCC) must stop treating Black turnout programs as an October line item. The report is unambiguous: late organizing money is wasted money. Time is irreplaceable. Every battleground budget should be re-scored this month against Ashley's 1 percent benchmark. If your spend on sustained Black voter contact, Black media, and Black-led organizations rounds to a rounding error, you are planning to lose. And frontline members outside the battlegrounds are not bystanders. Democratic-held districts averaged 41,000 fewer presidential votes than Republican-held ones in 2024. Members must drive participation in their own districts even without a competitive race at home.
**State parties** must build the Virginia model now: one coordinated table, top of the ticket to the bottom, with Black voter re-engagement as a core pillar rather than a constituency program bolted on in the fall. In Ohio, Michigan, North Carolina, Georgia, and Pennsylvania, that means paid organizers in Black neighborhoods this month, vote-by-mail and early vote education that accounts for new voting restrictions, and Black-led community partners funded as partners, not vendors.
**Candidate campaigns** must run at Black voters, not past them. The DNC's own research found Black voters frustrated with an economy that was not working for them and a party that would not say so. The lesson is not to soften the economic message. It is to sharpen it, deliver it through trusted local voices and Black media, and pair it with a visible, physical presence. Down-ballot Democrats outperformed the top of the ticket almost everywhere in 2024 and 2025. Do what they did: show up, localize, and ask for the vote directly.
## The bottom line
The DNC's instinct was to manage the story. Ours has to be to act on the substance. Rivera handed this party a map showing exactly where the erosion is happening and exactly what stops it. Ashley showed us the receipts on where the money did not go. Organizing works. Investment works. Virginia proved it eleven months ago, and The Collective PAC has been proving it for ten years.
Eighty days. The voters who stayed home in 2024 have not left us. But nobody gets to claim surprise in November if we spend 1 percent on them again and leave them on the couch.
It's time to get to work.

We mustn't lose. Not to these people.

The only thing that beats an organized socialist machine is an activated Right -- every door knocked, every ballot chased, every vote turned out.

name: Jenny Beth Martin, Tea Party Patriots Action
subject: She enlisted as Robert Shirtliff
body:
Meet Deborah Sampson, the soldier nobody could find out.
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org%2Ffoundation/1/010001a001be4061-ed61ff7d-5bc8-4b8b-a73c-929f4f31f33a-000000/bbH_O4VGdxFqR82lz4813GI0eOGZaSxQWs5w4hbpx0Y=452)Patriot–There are now seven episodes of Defiant Ones available, and [_the newest one went live yesterday_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.washingtontimes.com%2Fdefiant-ones%2Fdeborah-sampson%2F/1/010001a001be4061-ed61ff7d-5bc8-4b8b-a73c-929f4f31f33a-000000/ojiCz0rySQPN4hdbvBrjIgR5QmNf2z87DYoXREvUYa8=452).Let me tell you a little about that one.In the spring of 1782, a twenty-one-year-old woman in Massachusetts named Deborah Sampson decided she was going to fight for her country. Women were not allowed to. She was a weaver by trade, so she sewed herself a suit of men's clothes, walked into a recruiting station, and gave her name as Robert Shirtliff.She had tried this once before, under a different name, and a neighbor recognized her as she signed the papers.This time it held. The Continental Army took her, and she served seventeen months in the light infantry of the Fourth Massachusetts Regiment. She marched. She fought. She was wounded.And every day of those seventeen months, she was one bad moment away from being discovered.That is Episode 7, and I am not going to tell you how it ends. Go listen.**Here is everything available right now:**
* [_**Episode 1, Abigail Adams.**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.washingtontimes.com%2Fdefiant-ones%2Fabigail-adams%2F/1/010001a001be4061-ed61ff7d-5bc8-4b8b-a73c-929f4f31f33a-000000/dStv2JYKXPhKh30psvQuPrZFE11etAVJfeYmJGJU6s8=452)**** The letter that told the Founders to remember the ladies.
* [_**Episode 2, Prudence Wright.**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.washingtontimes.com%2Fdefiant-ones%2Fprudence-wright%2F/1/010001a001be4061-ed61ff7d-5bc8-4b8b-a73c-929f4f31f33a-000000/XehGChMe3otKg6peAFYvc6fEC77yjWZycfTR2ISkaBw=452)**** The women of Pepperell, Massachusetts, and the stand at Jewett Bridge.
* [_**Episode 3, Penelope Barker.**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.washingtontimes.com%2Fdefiant-ones%2Fpenelope-barker%2F/1/010001a001be4061-ed61ff7d-5bc8-4b8b-a73c-929f4f31f33a-000000/nDuCcy14LKZ9MatkFMaiI8A-FqxAcF-qc11eXOm7izI=452)**** Fifty-one women in Edenton, North Carolina, signed their names and sent them across the ocean for a king to read.
* [_**Episode 4, Phillis Wheatley.**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.washingtontimes.com%2Fdefiant-ones%2Fphillis-wheatley%2F/1/010001a001be4061-ed61ff7d-5bc8-4b8b-a73c-929f4f31f33a-000000/AhAV7qKwqvtZlZucNV2v0tPtgVJhoZML0ioSa8ZGsFQ=452)Kidnapped from West Africa as a child, enslaved in Boston, and read by George Washington.
* [_**Episode 5, Sybil Ludington.**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.washingtontimes.com%2Fdefiant-ones%2Fsybil-ludington%2F/1/010001a001be4061-ed61ff7d-5bc8-4b8b-a73c-929f4f31f33a-000000/RP6QMM6lsDvlmH3ipphCgEesFKgeerQp0mwnbIESMl0=452)**** The sixteen-year-old said to have ridden through the dark the night Danbury burned.
* [_**Episode 6, Two Kettles Together.**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.washingtontimes.com%2Fdefiant-ones%2Ftwo-kettles-together%2F/1/010001a001be4061-ed61ff7d-5bc8-4b8b-a73c-929f4f31f33a-000000/suzQDcq-kq7mBpK2qtWKhymiW1RLnTITF3gvZosKa54=452)**** An Oneida woman who went to the field at Oriskany, in a fight that split her own people.
* [_**Episode 7, Deborah Sampson.**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.washingtontimes.com%2Fdefiant-ones%2Fdeborah-sampson%2F/2/010001a001be4061-ed61ff7d-5bc8-4b8b-a73c-929f4f31f33a-000000/V7W7hxlOyyF1VdKrjDwCXu6Nwan-bDcbACG-n7ac4_E=452)**** New yesterday.

Each episode centers on one woman, so there is no wrong place to start. While you are there, request our free activity pack, built for children, so the young ones in your family have something to do with these stories too.Then come back next Thursday for the last one. The finale belongs to Agent 355, a woman who carried intelligence for General Washington's spy ring and who comes down to us without a name, known only by a number. It is a fitting way to close a series about women whose work was never meant to be written down.Tea Party Patriots Foundation is one of the partners behind this series, alongside Beautifully Flawed Productions, The Washington Times, and The Women In My World. Helping tell these stories as the country turns 250 has been one of the more satisfying things we have done this year.Eight women. Seven of them waiting for you tonight.In liberty,Jenny Beth Martin
Chairman, Tea Party Patriots Foundation P.S. If you have already been listening, do me one favor and forward this to somebody who has not. These stories were nearly lost once. They do not spread on their own.[CONTRIBUTE](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org%2Ffoundation%2Fdonate/1/010001a001be4061-ed61ff7d-5bc8-4b8b-a73c-929f4f31f33a-000000/mZ8vUeQ-VFnr_azT-sSAC1RzCWwWjW6p7SYB33Nt-0A=452) _This email list is a joint venture of the following separate organizations: Tea Party Patriots Action, Inc., Tea Party Patriots Foundation, and Tea Party Patriots Citizens Fund. body:
ICE may say they turned down the heat in Minnesota, but their constant harassment of my community continues.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2437%2E791427%2EE9c3Y0)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_aug26_abolish_ice_pet/?refcode=em260814-1-180&akid=2437%2E791427%2EE9c3Y0)
Friend — ICE may say they turned down the heat in Minnesota, but their constant harassment of my community continues.
**Last week, an ICE agent sat outside a town hall meeting with my constituents in a car with mismatched license plates.**
**This was a potential attempt to intimidate my neighbors, surveil one of Trump’s political opponents, and target the immigrant communities I serve for enforcement.**
Town hall meetings are a critically important way for me to engage with my constituents. They should be a place where anyone, regardless of immigration status, can come hear from their federal representative, ask important questions, and get connected with services without the fear of ICE violence.
The agent parked outside the meeting claimed to local law enforcement that they were there for a “drug enforcement operation” — but after everything ICE has done to Minnesotans, we have every right to have zero trust in this violent band of thugs.
They lied about the murder of Alex Pretti, they lied about the murder of Renee Good, and they have consistently lied about the brutality they unleashed on hundreds, if not thousands, of Minnesotans.
Friend, just this week Minnesotans went to the polls and nominated candidates up and down the ballot who have fought back against ICE’s occupation and are committed to dismantling this unaccountable, rogue agency.
I have been committed to abolishing ICE since Trump’s first term, and if we take the majority in Congress in November, I will put that fight front and center.
[**If you’re with me, sign my petition calling for ICE to be abolished. We can have a sensible, compassionate, and orderly immigration system without the chaos, violence, and lawlessness brought about by ICE. Your signature today helps us continue to build the grassroots movement against ICE:**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_aug26_abolish_ice_pet/?source=em260814-1-180&refcode2=2437.791427.E9c3Y0&akid=2437%2E791427%2EE9c3Y0)

In solidarity,
Ilhan Omar

I'd be doing you a real disservice if I didn't tell you exactly what's at stake:

The numbers we post after our deadline will be the first thing every political reporter, every Republican strategist, and every major donor looks at in the coming days. They're going to be asking one question: _Is there enough momentum to get Democrats to victory this November?_

Our answer has to be a resounding yes.

From Georgia to Texas to Ohio to right here in New Hampshire, there are battleground states all across the country that need our support. I’ve been doing my part to support where I can, but I need you in the fight with me.

Every dollar donated isn’t just an investment in this election cycle, but every election after that.

body:
Hoping to catch you before you check out of your inbox for the weekend.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137251866/640140879/510768709?refcode=email-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTIzMCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZGU3YWNlNC0xOTk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hFcI7-K53BjKn1yxuBnSkYU9OCvEKzm15nd9swQCLR8=) Hey there, we know you’re probably getting ready to check out of your inbox for the weekend, but we needed to share three important updates about our campaign to flip Michigan’s Fourth blue.
1. **Sean was officially elected as the Democratic nominee.** The real fight has begun, and we’re officially going head-to-head with Bill Huizenga and his millions of dollars of national GOP backing.

2. **The national GOP and Bill Huizenga are panicking about losing this seat.** They know polling shows Sean McCann up by 3 points, and election forecasters predict this race will be decided by less than a 1% margin. Lead Story · The Iran WarTRUMP CLAIMS 'TOTAL CONTROL' OF HORMUZ; IRAN SAYS THE STRAIT STAYS SHUTWhat's Happening
* President Trump declared the U.S. has **"total control" over the Strait of Hormuz** , wrote "I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT," and called the U.S. naval blockade "a wall of steel."
* Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi rejected the claim, saying Tehran considers the strait blocked until its conditions are met and that Trump "has long miscalculated due to intelligence failures."
* The United Arab Emirates said Iran attacked two of its vessels transiting the strait on Thursday, condemning what it called "flagrant" maritime violations.

The Situation
* Shipping data shows vessel traffic through the strait remains stalled, which does not yet square with the administration's claim of open, controlled passage.
* Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the administration is preparing new economic measures against Iran that he described as unprecedented in scale.
* The aircraft carrier USS George Washington is steaming toward the region to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has anchored the U.S. presence throughout the war.

The PerspectiveProjecting American strength at the world's most important chokepoint is the right instinct, and Iran's regime deserves no benefit of the doubt after years of proxy attacks and now direct strikes on civilian shipping. But confidence has to be matched by what the tankers actually do. If Trump says we control Hormuz, the measure is simple: commercial traffic flowing freely and safely. * U.S. District Judge Richard Stearns in Boston **dismissed the administration's lawsuit** alleging Harvard failed to protect Jewish and Israeli students from harassment.
* The suit, filed in March, did not plausibly show an ongoing violation of federal civil rights law, the judge ruled.
* Stearns called the alleged incidents "too isolated and episodic," noting most dated to 2023-24 campus protests over the war in Gaza.

The Situation
* The ruling is a setback for the administration's broader campaign to force policy changes at elite universities.
* A separate judge earlier ordered the government to unfreeze roughly $2.2 billion in federal grants to Harvard.
* The administration can appeal; the underlying fight over campus antisemitism and federal funding is far from settled.

* Two softer inflation reports this week — the CPI and the PPI — have investors betting the Fed **won't raise rates at its September meeting**.

The Situation

The economy lost 23,000 jobs in July — the first negative report since February — while unemployment slipped to a low 4.1%. * Rebounding gas prices and the war with Iran could push August inflation data back up, analysts caution. The PerspectiveCooling prices are real relief for families who have been squeezed for years, and a low 4.1% unemployment rate says the underlying economy still has spine. But a pause is not a victory lap. With inflation stuck above target, a wobbling July jobs number, and gas prices climbing on the back of the Iran war, the Fed is right to stay cautious rather than declare the fight won. The honest read is encouraging but incomplete: the trend is friendly, the job isn't finished, and one good week doesn't retire the risk. | ⚡ The Bottom LineToday's thread is the gap between what leaders declare and what the facts confirm: a strait that Washington calls controlled while the tankers sit still, a lawsuit that voiced a real grievance but couldn't clear the bar, sailors whose exhaustion demands answers rather than spin, and an inflation report that's genuinely better but not yet finished. Strength and honesty aren't opposites — the strongest position is the one that holds up when the ships move, the docket closes, the crews come home, and next month's numbers land. Milo has won at the Royal Windsor Horse Show eight years in a row, including after going fully blind. He's now preparing to enter , often described as "ballet on horseback," where he would compete against sighted horses. Megan believes he could become the first blind horse to compete in a dressage event. Megan, 28, who has owned Milo since he was three, says their bond made the comeback possible. name: Scott Peters
subject: They are running out the clock on 9,000 San Diegans
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Scott Peters for Congress
body:
15 days. Then 70 days. Now people are losing their jobs waiting.
---
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137253493/640145006/586034392?refcode2=SP_EM_PT_180DO_260812_1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODA2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiY2QwOGQ5NC0xYzk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=SC6agUIDoSqFVtEgKjzqp-MfTAoglrd9capieQ5r9lY=&emci=ac8ca890-7696-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=bcd08d94-1c98-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=5258741) Peter,

In 2025, the median wait for a DACA renewal was 15 days. By February of this year it was 70 days - an increase of more than 400%.

Nationwide, roughly **54,000 renewals are sitting in limbo right now.**

Right now, my office is handling the highest volume of immigration casework I have seen in my entire time in Congress. A firefighter, a radiation technology technician, a teacher. All of them follow the rules. All of them are waiting; 4-6 weeks at a minimum.

One San Diego woman who managed 150 people applied three months early, heard nothing, and lost her job - along with about $25,000 in unvested stock and bonuses.

Nearly 9,000 DACA recipients call San Diego home. They work here, they pay taxes here, and for most of them this country is the only one they have ever known - the average recipient is 33 and has lived here for 27 years. **Dreamers contribute an estimated $968 million to San Diego's economy every year.**

And this is not a close call with the public: a recent poll reported 81% of Americans - including 56% of Republicans - support giving Dreamers a path to citizenship.

**I spoke out when Donald Trump attacked DACA the first time. I am still speaking out, because our work is not over. And we still do not have answers to the simplest questions: how does this administration plan to clear the backlog it created - and are DACA recipients being detained because of the lag?**

clean_body: 15 days. Then 70 days. Now people are losing their jobs waiting. | | Peter, In 2025, the median wait for a DACA renewal was 15 days. By February of this year it was 70 days - an increase of more than 400%. Nationwide, roughly 54,000 renewals are sitting in limbo right now. Right now, my office is handling the highest volume of immigration casework I have seen in my entire time in Congress. A firefighter, a radiation technology technician, a teacher. All of them follow the rules. All of them are waiting; 4-6 weeks at a minimum. One San Diego woman who managed 150 people applied three months early, heard nothing, and lost her job - along with about $25,000 in unvested stock and bonuses. Nearly 9,000 DACA recipients call San Diego home. They work here, they pay taxes here, and for most of them this country is the only one they have ever known - the average recipient is 33 and has lived here for 27 years. Dreamers contribute an estimated $968 million to San Diego's economy every year. And this is not a close call with the public: a recent poll reported 81% of Americans - including 56% of Republicans - support giving Dreamers a path to citizenship. I spoke out when Donald Trump attacked DACA the first time. I am still speaking out, because our work is not over. name: OnePA Team
subject: RE: Big Tech billionaires did not see this coming
body:
Pennsylvania organizers changed the debate over taxing Big Tech. Now corporations are counting on lawmakers to stop the momentum. | |
---
Peter, Big Tech billionaires are hoping Pennsylvania’s victory in the state House goes no further. They know the Digital Ad Tax passed the House because working people organized, developed leaders, confronted lawmakers, and changed what elected officials believed was politically possible. Companies like Amazon, Meta, TikTok, Google, and Microsoft are trying to stop that momentum. Their business model generates billions of dollars by tracking everyday people and selling access to us through targeted advertisements. They want outdated tax codes to remain exactly as they are: working people and local communities carry the responsibility for funding public services while massive technology corporations extract profits. **We c****annot allow corporate lobbyists to stop Pennsylvania from finishing the job or prevent lawmakers in other states from taking on Big Tech too.** [**Tell your State Senator to follow the House’s lead and pass the Digital Ad Tax now.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38DNVGHNeES2F9IVxdkY1DIlUGMjix-Ugazl9P8r3ofMTEKG8B5xv2lL-JCQ2tzezoSUoBdaXXHgNtngdggURP-TuDB8JIqzlJM3BuAPFk5IgsU-4qSRk4nrO7av7bt7q7yGKBi8MPIy5mlyVXlTln3JsB5OClukgn7c4KnXAVcknJ1gGtlC_TD9iWMqdSzwLMUNELfNmDoB5jkoyg-8ptJPVaQ0yiZ2MzXgtasCuIy3ps7c7nNf7toPOym6QRHi46_6BtTBl93W0de9gAajbzhiWDgobFse_tKNOYSOySJrOSaCv2qJVKv2b__rD9fF1Y_famUSiq9wb59YuFxhXrXBIMKcB-1N3VJH4zYc54rZj-lux3dbmCW_ZBSOlQ8YWyf__e7fx7Z25nwolkXJYBd_U9RqEu2-0eyqtz85k4Gfw/4t6/Kc9p_guIR8qs2ynaPJ3Dpw/h0/h001.sDn6e3J7Mx136-wj-NHVLPM0MkJAw9jS0PtXUhp__SE) | | [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38DNVGHNeES2F9IVxdkY1DIlUGMjix-Ugazl9P8r3ofMTEKG8B5xv2lL-JCQ2tzezoSUoBdaXXHgNtngdggURP-TuDB8JIqzlJM3BuAPFk5IgsU-4qSRk4nrO7av7bt7q7yGKBi8MPIy5mlyVXlTln3JsB5OClukgn7c4KnXAVcko8FtWFAYcnfqZqYQiQKmK4X9DvFsGrTMlSHrkNssj61iGWXsw02hSGCTPjCgD0NIJ8KwGGUDf_z6o2J074fqxVkvptRTkl1fJl0-PKgcajKW65smyzgnoiRk7A_6IZQ67sJhF47nIMHBpMV616wt8T3X_OXOXoN5UDJdmPNLHoCMZ2FMBnosNiccEn9eMIStSVCV_vjJOy0wBgkQDf842q4HMofj2zzQ72LyrOjrt2sf6pj7S3HN9RK2jgZtKm3Cw/4t6/Kc9p_guIR8qs2ynaPJ3Dpw/h1/h001.F4CyiE3a5D_AR90WS1oS4KWENROK0fXOITOVR9bAFXM)

**Far too many politicians claim they face only two choices when budgets are tight: cut programs or raise taxes on working people.**
**Those are not the only choices.** Lawmakers can tax the corporations and billionaires that have spent years accumulating wealth while our schools, transit systems, healthcare programs, and neighborhoods are denied the investments they need.
Pennsylvania organizers are proving that this movement can bring people together and move lawmakers in both parties. We’re building support for the Digital Ad tax by naming the real divide clearly: working people on one side and billionaires using their money to shape government on the other.

he's right| | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137254070/640146943/724950626?refcode=260814-agree-mj&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MDU1NTRjNy0xZjk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VFgen1pScqxLRD2oUMN64lc3aljhxpcvFmf2byoY8qI=)

I don't agree with Speaker Mike Johnson very often. But he's right about one thing. When he came to Southwest Washington last month to raise money for my opponent, he told the room that Washington's 3rd District will decide who controls the House. He's right. There are only a handful of true toss-up seats in the country, and this is one of them. That's why the Speaker of the House came all the way to Southwest Washington to raise money for my opponent.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137254071/640146944/724950626?refcode=260814-agree-mj&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MDU1NTRjNy0xZjk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VFgen1pScqxLRD2oUMN64lc3aljhxpcvFmf2byoY8qI=)
---
It's why Republican outside groups have already spent or reserved nearly $7 million in advertising against me here. And it's why national Republicans are prepared to spend even more before Election Day. They've done the math. They know how much this seat matters. So do I. I've won here twice by earning the support of people who don't always agree with me, but know I'll put Southwest Washington ahead of either political party. I don't take corporate PAC money. I don't answer to party leadership. And I'm not interested in becoming another reliable vote for whoever happens to be in charge in Washington, D.C. That's exactly the kind of representation national Republicans are spending millions to replace. Mike Johnson came here because Republicans believe winning this seat could keep them in control of the House. I think that's a pretty good reason for us to fight like hell to keep it. University systems have been completely captured by radical ideology, but they're not setting a dangerous new precedent: Making political endorsements. The American Association of University Professors (AAUP) broke its 110 year long tradition of not making national campaign endorsements. Who did they choose to back? None other than the Muslim socialist Senate candidate, **[Abdul El-Sayed](https://substack.com/redirect/c0221381-777e-424f-a00b-f7b2882a001f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
[| | | | | Josh Kalla
---
@j_kalla
I am not an AAUP member, but I think it is a really bad idea for the American Association of University Professors to be endorsing candidates, especially in a factional Democratic primary.
| 2:22 PM * Jul 30, 2026 * 485K Views33 Replies * 66 Reposts * 706 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/fb3d87ab-a9ad-4009-bd49-61e0c12abcef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The AAUP released a **[statement](https://substack.com/redirect/87f0bea8-1952-4b27-b3d8-a1a2647da834?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that praised Sayed for championing "debt-free and tuition-free education," something that he has been advocating for since 2018. The AAUP has simultaneously launched their own **[initiative](https://substack.com/redirect/706d23c2-b490-4b8a-850b-3d3929b1b5cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for free college, claiming that doing so would "counter the far-right's extremist attacks on higher education." They argue that doing so would favor black and hispanic applicants, who have historically higher rates of faulting on their student loans. The AAUP blames this disproportionate debt burden on the Trump administration's cuts from DEI programs. The Department of Justice has determined that DEI grants are **[unconstitutional](https://substack.com/redirect/2af14197-d609-4d03-9476-85d37c01a6ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and that sex-based preferential treatment can be considered a violation of the 1964 Civil Rights Act.
Their new platform would also allow liberal professors to make curriculum decisions, boxing out oversight in a communist style form of "shared governance." They specifically cite that 54 faculty have been suspended or terminated since fall 2025. They state that these professors were placed on watch lists where they dealt with "intimidation" and "efforts to limit and control their speech." Several of these fired professors were promoting radical ideologies. **[Dr. Tom Alter](https://substack.com/redirect/7cfd8b52-674a-4981-8d3e-63de44269195?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** was fired after speaking at a revolutionary socialist convention and making comments that some believed were inciting violence. **[Professor Melissa McCoul](https://substack.com/redirect/acd00e74-43fd-475f-98b1-fa442a0fff2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** was fired for making her Texas A&M students read a book featuring a 12-year old nonbinary purple unicorn.
* * *
* * *

* * *
* * *
However, most of those professors faced consequences for publicly celebrating the assassination of Charlie Kirk. One, a law **[professor](https://substack.com/redirect/77aaefbe-ee56-4b72-bb1a-e4012aa4c38c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at the University of Arkansas, likened people mourning Kirk's death to members of the Klu Klux Klan. Several of her fellow faculty members initially suggested that she should keep her job but receive a warning, although she was fired after a month of paid suspension. Professors from Florida Atlantic, Tennessee, and Georgia posted distasteful comments about Kirk's death, ultimately getting themselves fired. Multiple professors at Clemson University were also fired for social media posts celebrating his death. The AUUP's resolution for tuition-free colleges would allow professors like these to run rampant and easily secure tenure.
In the AAUP's endorsement of Sayed, they state their hopes that he will "defend the rights of students and faculty to speak out on political issues, question authority, and engage in peaceful protest." Sayed has a long history of engaging in protests, but they weren't actually "peaceful." In **[2018](https://substack.com/redirect/46fce6a8-811c-4f5e-8779-1a591d53a64e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , Sayed participated in a sit-in at a McDonalds, advocating for an increased minimum wage. He and 16 other protesters were arrested for disorderly conduct, to which he pleaded guilty. Sayed also held a leadership position for the group Michigan United. In **[May 2020](https://substack.com/redirect/3783d51b-b80e-40de-8b8e-2dd93eadcd29?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ,** the group held a violent protest that turned into a riot. Cops were attacked and hospitalized, and one person was killed. By endorsing Sayed, the AAUP is inviting violent protests onto college campuses.

The AAUP's break in historic precedence marks a new turn away from educational integrity towards activism. The group's President, Todd Wolfson, said in **[2025](https://substack.com/redirect/f8d873b0-044f-41d9-96ea-4f1f22025c5a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that they would be committing to "militant action." At their **[June](https://substack.com/redirect/b8f8091a-0f8f-4a12-b581-5a628a6c6233?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/b8f8091a-0f8f-4a12-b581-5a628a6c6233?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[2026](https://substack.com/redirect/b8f8091a-0f8f-4a12-b581-5a628a6c6233?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** meeting, they concluded that "defense alone" would not be sufficient for them anymore. They voted to pursue DEI programs, fight for a "mulitracial, inclusive democracy," and double down on socializing "healthcare, housing, education, and economic security." The AAUP made it clear that they hoped to pursue activism above all else- Which makes Abdul El-Sayed their perfect partner in crime.

body:
I can’t win this race without you. Today, I’m asking you to make your first donation to my campaign.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1122&source=&t=1&akid=2697%2E124072%2EScrmD_)
| | | |
---
Peter,
As one of the most engaged supporters of my U.S. Senate campaign in North Carolina, your involvement has had a real impact on our ability to stay competitive in this fight. Thank you.
I hope you know how grateful I am for your time and attention – [**_and today, I’m asking you to take the next step with your first contribution of $5._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1122&amount=5&t=9&akid=2697%2E124072%2EScrmD_) Here’s why:
Experts say Senate control will be decided in North Carolina, so between now and November, keeping up our momentum day by day is key to our success. With our August mid-month fundraising deadline in just over 24 hours, that is especially true today.
**However, grassroots donations fell off significantly after our July end-of-month deadline, and my finance team has had to make the tough decision to lower our projection for August.**
That’s a big problem when recent polling shows that my lead has tightened to just 4 points and when the Senate GOP’s top super PAC has gone live with false attack ads against me.
If we have to make the massive budget cuts we’re currently deliberating, we’ll put our chances of flipping this seat at risk. **That’s why my team has set a $1 million fundraising goal before tomorrow’s mid-month deadline.**
[**_So Peter, I’m asking you to chip in and help us make today our biggest fundraising day of the month yet so we can turn things around. I’d be grateful for your $5 or anything you can spare. # DNC Coalitions Partner Briefing
---
| | Dear Partner,
We’re inviting you to our monthly **Partner Briefing on Wednesday, August 19, from 4:00 - 4:30 PM ET**! This is your opportunity to connect with the DNC team for an exclusive update on our momentum and strategic initiatives. Here is what we’ll be covering:
* **🗳️ Election Overview** : Get the latest on topline results and an inside look at how we’re building crucial infrastructure.
* **👥 Coalitions Impact & Action: **Discover the latest on our key engagement efforts.
* **🤝 Program Engagement:** Discover our latest programs and how you can get involved.

**EVENT DETAILS:**
* **Date:** Wednesday, July 22 2026
* **Time:** 4:00 - 4:30 PM ET
* **Location:** ZOOM Webinar
* **Registration Link:** [win.dnc.org/august-partner-briefing](https://us.list-manage.com/5T191vfFdk2?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)

| | | Peter, it’s Brian Poindexter, the Working Families Party champion running to flip Ohio’s 7th Congressional District from red to blue. It's official: I’m taking on Max Miller this November. The deadline has passed for him to withdraw, and Miller is locked into the ballot. That means that this November 3, the path to taking back the House runs through Ohio, where voters will choose between one of Trump’s favorite aides with a long history of alleged violence, and me — a proud union ironworker, girl dad, and public servant ready to work for working people. **This is a race we can’t afford to lose, Peter.[If I can count on your support in the fight to take down Max Miller and build a government that stands up for the working class, split a donation between my campaign and the Working Families Party today.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9fQfKXA1ciLJIqN3tvJIT11Occ8cEE2yRXRrFtfB35lo4DsJ7QknJ5ISKYLlDOZ3NP_mimeuqmfbuxwfYhaQHBK_sJzZPYWqmkzlfYOmHFRfFNYq99_20k6SYLtFlUZAixhgEa3K0m6ogKwONCANIbNcPUivlbyfRk3NSS1vuavDcBlbELwJ4AN5DEtnm04jK1dA3wDIttBa3V08WjLj2mmLqaHPMHhlD49Krkzfbwk-2Kx9xJFXqchKcDXHebFFL8FF8o9rBFVAjgFlFBNqc3YoNb1OCwhYUcns8o4UDZE0/4t6/uBWyf5mVSTahf1w07NTVUw/h0/h001.imWHlmyEY0xBsfDahaovB_8fONBelWfkTcTaoEmKeDc)** **[Donate $10 »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9fQfKXA1ciLJIqN3tvJIT11Occ8cEE2yRXRrFtfB35lo97PXu_Fm1PmszZD-crrwHIj8Shn0_u3pMk0ThzWmMt1J_s6NeHCAytl2DL6gWgBkvc4TPNjWhK0POSxEbnm8t0UU2e6bZ2a-UyPIh7wjvMSK-EYpVFeaJLFILMYOOYPhfCrLg6YnhKk0MI5PbZ1lZuG_fUoPJd3uyyWUMkyy0uQ6BuSJzKXS3APQe8cJGAk89Y43pcwJ15wZuddzG4mOcHjnKR0eZvOmzaRjEnOg2celk4RDfGDaWk5gqJEJlb0U/4t6/uBWyf5mVSTahf1w07NTVUw/h1/h001.Uxrbs5ah5p1XJLT3dZBG5QJ8NjpVw-_Alr6_4GFZpnE)** I fight for workers because I am a worker. Whether on a machine shop floor, walking a beam on a Cleveland skyscraper, or sitting down with a resident to solve a local issue, I live and breathe working-class values and will bring that pro-worker mentality to the halls of Congress. That's what this campaign has been about from day one. My opponent Max Miller, on the other hand, was born the heir of a multimillionaire real estate dynasty. His career in politics, cozying up to and defending Donald Trump, was handed to him on a silver platter. **As more and more voters learn about what our working class movement is fighting for, along with my opponent’s moral bankruptcy, the polls are moving in our direction.** A recent GOP-commissioned poll had us up by double digits. But Miller and his buddy Trump are refusing to back down, and now that he’s officially locked into the ballot, they're going to throw everything they have at this district to defeat us. **We need your support today to ensure that we can beat Max Miller in November and send a real working class champion to Congress.[Will you split a donation between my campaign and the Working Families Party today?](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9fQfKXA1ciLJIqN3tvJIT11Occ8cEE2yRXRrFtfB35lo4DsJ7QknJ5ISKYLlDOZ3NtIietTUYWKnKVUT6wxglkPj4cpHX0T-zCIKSwtVr0dG2xDyDymJxz87ociNyDihELIKMkvSMqqPRIlAkb_yLbtxdLMqP4Jk1RrQsH70ht4uHSS11zluRwpY9LamRY1UDs3eljvUxmcYWBo6TDzTJNszK-wIhbiczNPWaQBfwIBCkkFFawNFH_GVtzKzPXcTZM0WdJqpCW4of657TJQbVg4AU5X975ldI4YerLlpqglM/4t6/uBWyf5mVSTahf1w07NTVUw/h2/h001.EKySXJruZkoAdPKio6Zg9cZUVi5pYDzpqaED6gL1cM0)** **[Donate $10 »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9fQfKXA1ciLJIqN3tvJIT11Occ8cEE2yRXRrFtfB35lo97PXu_Fm1PmszZD-crrwHklTHYJ-oyw8_w41RG-QbhCegvmgCtpKZC-e9uXAVIaibdA6gCc-1F8LRB1jTbfpmygRKfoPG__poQoZ9L8DuWZpxqstrINqtdem8pn7FrqcdBRZGU8xPoDkyzN3ONpSsOLCNxVZgJW1vBu1Dg9jMgmGJMeFqtpSTWocjgP4QoaFWsvBBJTshXiKSk6_jnCfgIdLHKHyk2cY85RY3lZGmD5MQ-SAH0tWFbntP1u9oYMc/4t6/uBWyf5mVSTahf1w07NTVUw/h3/h001.l_Jj25kmZyUT-fWjgaYZESC5paqnSWS11dfa0jcpid4)** In solidarity, Brian Poindexter

clean_body: Fox26 Houston: Texas county accused of changing voting maps after primary elections| | | This is simple: Galveston County pulling this off could embolden other Texas jurisdictions to tweak election maps after seeing primary results in order to boost partisan advantages in the general election. Then other states would follow suit. Then this somehow becomes standard practice for opponents of voting rights nationwide. = | | | | = Opponents of voting rights are at it again, Team. Their latest move to skew election results comes in Texas, where it looks like Galveston County officials admitted to trying to use a new map in November that was different than the boundaries used for election districts in their primary back in March. This spilled out in a recent court case, after new maps were passed by the county at the end of July. Galveston's primary in March used maps drawn in 2021 that voters were familiar with. Galveston County filed in court recently to use the new maps, passed in July, for November, changing the boundaries on voters and, in some cases, swapping voters away from the candidates they voted for in March's primary election. This is yet another dirty trick from the vote suppressors , this time at the local level instead of a state legislature or Congress. It shows just how deep the rot goes, with local officials willing to bend lines and break the rules to choose their voters instead of letting voters choose who best represents them. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | = | | | The impact of these changes is clear: Voters in Galveston County will see elections that they were supposed to vote in delayed two extra years, extending the terms of elected officials that voters may want out. Making this move between the primary and the general election also prevents candidates from knowing what district they were running in and limits the ability of potential candidates to immediately run in these new districts if they had wanted to. Let's be real, though. This isn't just about one county in Texas, or the whole state. This is about setting a legal precedent to do this elsewhere. We've seen it for years: The vote suppressors try a tactic like this on a local level and win, which sets a legal standard to try it somewhere else. Then other counties follow the same playbook, extending this tactic statewide. From there, just like the voter suppression bills we saw copied from state to state, opponents of voting rights push into other states, like a row of dominoes, until a new legal standard exists across the country. That's why this fight, as seemingly small or disconnected from our daily lives as it may seem, is so important. Peter, my opponent has it backwards. He wants to make it easier for criminals to carry guns in public but harder to keep guns off our streets.
**That is not a future I'm willing to accept as governor of Maryland.**
_In three years, we've seen historic reductions in violent crime. Homicides are at their lowest level in decades. Baltimore is on track to have its lowest number of murders since 1970._
Dan Cox would reverse all of it. Less safety. Less accountability. More guns in the wrong hands.
And it just got worse. In June, the Supreme Court struck down campaign spending rules for national parties, and Republicans are ready to pour in money to roll back the progress we've made — from bringing jobs to our state to making our communities safer.
**[We can’t let that happen. We need to make sure we’re able to fight back. Can you chip in today to help us protect what we’ve built and keep fighting for every Marylander?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260814-3.iLzqDL&refcode=em-20260814-3&t=2&akid=1751%2E1086043%2Es9EjSx)**
