subject: There's another shock poll, Peter
body:
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, look at this:
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260814_3_ampoll.diKXyY&refcode=em20260814-1829&amount=5&t=1&akid=1829%2E299639%2EQin5TJ)
Nine weeks ago, this same poll had us trailing Greg Abbott by 6 points. **Now, that gap is down to 1.**
This is a completely separate survey than the Fox News poll that broke recently — Texas Pulse, conducted by Texas A&M’s Bush School for Government — _and it found the exact same thing_ : **Abbott 46%, me at 45%.**
Three different pollsters showing identical results in the same week is not a fluke. It’s a trend. **[Chip in right now to help us take the lead in this race.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260814_3_ampoll.diKXyY&refcode=em20260814-1829&amount=5&t=2&akid=1829%2E299639%2EQin5TJ)**
Here's what’s changed since the June poll showing us down 6: Texans are getting to know me. In June, more than half of voters didn’t know enough about me to have an opinion. Now it’s less than a third. And the more they learn, the more they like what they see. **My favorability has climbed from a net +13 to a net +18 in just two months.**
Meanwhile, Abbott’s numbers are going the other way. His approval rating is underwater, 47-51%. His favorability is underwater, 46-50%. Twelve years as governor, and Texans are done.
I don’t need to tell you why. You’re living it. Rising grocery bills, rising premiums, rising property taxes. Data centers flooding our state. And a governor who’s spent over a decade protecting the people at the top instead of the Texans footing the bill.
**We have momentum. We do not have the resources to match it — not yet, not without your help.** Abbott’s campaign has nearly $70 million sitting in the bank, and they are going to spend every dollar of it trying to make sure Texans who are ready for change don’t show up in November.
**[Can you chip in $5 right now to help us keep closing this gap and finally defeat Greg Abbott in November?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260814_3_ampoll.diKXyY&refcode=em20260814-1829&amount=5&t=3&akid=1829%2E299639%2EQin5TJ)**

Three pollsters had us down one single point this week. We can win this, I feel it in my bones. Now let’s make it happen.
Gina

Team, 91 years ago today, President FDR signed Social Security into law. Social Security is a lifeline for Hudson Valley seniors. For generations, it has represented a simple promise: if you work hard and pay into the system, the benefits you earned will be there when you need them. But now, thanks to Donald Trump, that promise is under threat. After he sent DOGE after the Social Security Administration, the Social Security retirement trust fund is projected to run short in 2032. clean_body: Pat says NO | = Team, 91 years ago today, President FDR signed Social Security into law. Social Security is a lifeline for Hudson Valley seniors. For generations, it has represented a simple promise: if you work hard and pay into the system, the benefits you earned will be there when you need them. But now, thanks to Donald Trump, that promise is under threat. After he sent DOGE after the Social Security Administration, the Social Security retirement trust fund is projected to run short in 2032. Without action, Hudson Valley seniors could see their benefit checks cut by up to $500 per month by 2032. Pat is fighting back. To commemorate this anniversary, he’s renewing his fight to pass the Protecting Social Security Act — landmark legislation to ensure Americans’ earned benefits cannot be cut, even if the trust fund reaches insolvency. = Social Security is our seniors’ money. body:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137257321/640157489/274653739?refcode=AU_MTH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260814_PM2_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYzRmMzQ5YS0yYjk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=GbTtBK-dIMt79IA5z96D0zmc9HLBdd7u_RoOTtgg8pM=) Friend, in almost 250 years, there’s never been a Native woman serving in the US Senate. **It’s time to change that.** I’m Peggy Flanagan, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota. I am Ojibwe and a proud member of the White Earth Nation. My family is the Wolf Clan. The mission of my clan is to never leave anyone behind — and that’s been my guiding principle. I am the descendant of people who were forced off their land onto the White Earth reservation. I am the relative of residential boarding school survivors. I am the daughter of a man who always spoke truth to power for the good of the Anishinaabe people. I’m thinking of my daughter — who just got her first jingle dress — and whether or not she will see Indigenous women in all parts of our government. **Right now, there are no Native voices in the US Senate._If I win this race, we can change that._** **[It's high time that all our communities have a seat at the table. If you agree, will you pitch in $10 or whatever you can to power my campaign and Martin Heinrich’s and help me make history?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137257324/640157492/274653739?amount=10&refcode=AU_MTH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260814_PM2_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYzRmMzQ5YS0yYjk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=GbTtBK-dIMt79IA5z96D0zmc9HLBdd7u_RoOTtgg8pM=)** | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137257328/640157495/274653739?amount=10&refcode=AU_MTH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260814_PM2_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYzRmMzQ5YS0yYjk4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=GbTtBK-dIMt79IA5z96D0zmc9HLBdd7u_RoOTtgg8pM=)

Too often, Native voices are ignored or erased in the halls of power.
That’s how we get awful so-called leaders like Donald Trump and J.D. Vance, who called Indigenous Peoples' Day a “fake holiday” and said that Native land was “enemy territory.”
My Ojibwe name means 'Speaks in a Loud and Clear Voice woman.' So I’m using that voice to call out MAGA extremism — loudly and clearly.
But I can’t do it alone. I need your help to build a campaign strong enough to cut through the noise. body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson]
Growing up in Allagash and spending years working 80-hour weeks in the woods to make ends meet, I know firsthand what working Mainers need from our government.
And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. And I’m sick of it.
My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger.
This weekend, I officially earned the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate. Now it’s time to defeat Susan Collins and her billionaire backers. So I’m asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to become a Founding Donor to my campaign right now and help us win the most important Senate race in the country. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson]
DONATE TO DEFEAT SUSAN COLLINS AND FLIP THE SENATE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson]
Let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me.
When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.
After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.
I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.

body:
We know you’re probably getting ready to log off for the weekend.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137258172/640159248/-629675555?refcode=email-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDY3MjEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMDNiM2M2ZTYtMmM5OC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=HMdIuJD2gAsXePwLMRien6iOYwKNceD2f0Jx9lxKsYo=) We know you’re probably getting ready to log off for the weekend. But before you do, we hope you’ll read this: In 2024, Janelle Bynum flipped Oregon’s 5th District from red to blue by an extremely narrow margin. Since then, she’s gotten to work delivering for Oregonians — from passing legislation to lower housing costs to helping small businesses get ahead. This year, she’s one of the most vulnerable Democrats up for re-election. And her race could decide control of the House. **Here’s the issue: There are 6,000 fewer registered Democrats in our district since November 2024. Janelle only won by 10,945 votes that year.** _So if you do the math, it means OR-05 could come to razor-thin margins again this year. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. When the Senate is deadlocked, when a crisis demands calm instead of chaos, when someone needs to actually get something DONE instead of just yelling about it on cable news - they call Susan.She teaches steadfast leadership. She doesn't just practice it; she models it for the next generation of Senators who are watching how she operates.If we lose Maine, we don't just lose a seat. We lose the one person in that building whom colleagues trust to hold the line when it matters most. We lose the leadership that other Senators have learned from for years. And we hand the Senate majority and the stability it provides to the other side.We refuse to let that happen without a fight.[Can you step up right now with $10, $25, or whatever you can give to make sure Maine doesn't lose Susan - and America doesn't lose her leadership?](https://trk.emails.susancollinsformaine._g)

State Rep. Rhett Marques credited U.S. Sen. Katie Britt as a major force behind his primary win Tuesday night, saying he “would not be standing right here” without her support.

Marques (R-Enterprise) secured the Republican nomination for Alabama’s newly drawn 2nd Congressional District with 50% of the vote in a six-candidate field.

Addressing supporters after the victory, Marques first thanked President Donald Trump for giving his campaign a late boost with his endorsement before turning to Britt, who backed Marques early in his congressional bid.

U.S. Sen. Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) introduced new legislation aimed at ensuring the military personnel responsible for protecting America’s interests in space are prepared for potential conflicts.

Britt and U.S. Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) introduced the bipartisan Space Superiority Readiness Act of 2026, which would expand wargaming, modeling, simulation and training for U.S. Space Force Guardians.

Wargaming uses simulated exercises to prepare military personnel for potential conflicts. The expanded programs would focus on strengthening Space Force readiness and establishing U.S. space superiority.

Senator Katie Britt was presented the Legislative Conservationist of the Year Award at the 2026 Alabama Wildlife Federation Governor’s Conservation Achievement Awards banquet, while Chris Blankenship was presented the Conservationist of the Year Award.

The Alabama Wildlife Federation, or AWF, held the banquet, co-sponsored by Alabama Power Company and PowerSouth Energy, on Friday, August 7, at The Marriott Legends at Capitol Hill in Prattville. Governor Kay Ivey provided a congratulatory video prepared specifically for the 2026 award recipients.

I didn’t run for Senate to sit on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and proud to stand for every corner of Alabama—our cities, small towns, and rural communities alike. **I’m rooted in faith, built on family, and committed to making Alabama stronger and better for generations to come.** Alabama is a place of hard work, strong values, and unyielding independence. But the Left is trying to tear that all down. I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for every Alabamian who feels forgotten and left behind. Whether it’s securing our borders, protecting our children, or defending our way of life, I’m here fighting for Alabama’s future. **This fight isn’t easy, but it's worth it. And I’m not going anywhere.** Will you stand with me?

# **Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to federal stalking charge in Thompson killing**
Luigi Mangione **[pleaded guilty](https://substack.com/redirect/ee39413b-7d02-410d-b0d1-125841cecfbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Friday in Manhattan federal court to stalking charges, admitting he used a 3D-printed gun to shoot UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in December 2024 after posing as an investor to learn the location of the company's conference. He faces up to life in prison, with sentencing set for Dec. 18.

body:
This is a textbook example of a rigged system.
#
Elon Musk is back at it:
His super PAC is preparing to drop over **$100 million** to boost Republicans in the midterms, targeting key House and Senate races in at least eight states.
After he was the biggest donor in the 2024 election by spending close to _$300 million_ , he’s doubling down on undermining our democracy.
This has been the right’s plan all along. Because their attacks on the working class are deeply unpopular, they’re spending millions to crush working-class fighters across the country instead of winning with ideas.
It’s a textbook example of a rigged system. Elon will spend millions to elect politicians who will help him make billions. Alexandria has never backed down from the billionaires trying to buy our elections, and she’s not stopping now. She’s building a movement to take them on with a new way of doing politics — one that challenges the status quo and puts working people first.
**But Alexandria can’t do this work alone. She needs a movement alongside her.** _And you are a critical part of that very movement._

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: Did you catch this? Trump smuggled off AF1 👀
body:
Plus: Nobody seems to be running for Governor right now | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/XCysg4sH0Oj?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
A catering truck pulled up to Air Force One in Turkey. The President got in. The press flew out on the plane he wasn't on! Wild story.

Plus, [Jay McCleskey is with us for this special episode.](https://us.list-manage.com/y8CCA1M4cdK?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e) We’re covering the quietest governor's race anyone can remember, and the body cam footage from a 13-year-old's rescue that every newsroom in the state reported as an “Albuquerque man.” Plus one of the best universities in the country just stopped giving freshmen grades.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1B1wgNUnvmH?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | 🔥 **TRUMP SNUCK OFF AIR FORCE ONE IN TURKEY — THE PRESS FLEW THE DECOY**
The cameras caught him walking up the stairs in Ankara. Minutes later a catering truck pulled away from the far side of the plane.
Scott Jennings went on CNN and said the story raised the hair on the back of his neck. He also explained what level of threat it takes before anyone makes that call.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/woKzMa1mB2p?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| | 👮 **THE STORY EVERY NEWSROOM FILED AS "ALBUQUERQUE MAN"**
Jay McCleskey brings the body cam footage from a 13-year-old girl's rescue in Rio Rancho.
Every outlet in the state reported a 34-year-old “Albuquerque man”. Jay has what the officers saw. There's one detail in that video that changes the whole story, and not a single newsroom included it.
He's now suing Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham's office to keep this footage coming. Wait until you hear what the legislature has planned for next session.
▶️ [**WATCH BREAKING BODY CAMS**](https://us.list-manage.com/C68CnazAabe?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)**

**🏛️**THE SILENT GOVERNOR RACE**
Six weeks from early voting, Deb Haaland isn't attacking. Gregg Hull isn't on TV. Krysty can't find a yard sign anywhere. What the heck?!
Jay says the silence is the most dangerous signal in this race, and he explains why quiet from a campaign with that much money should scare you more than an attack ad would.
Then he says something about Hull's own poll we did not expect him to say out loud...

📚 **MICHIGAN JUST STOPPED GIVING FRESHMEN GRADES**
One of the best public universities in the country will show first-semester students "pass" or "no credit" and nothing else. Krysty connects it to a state where law school graduates can't pass the easiest bar exam in America, and where APS just gave kids a "soft launch" instead of a first day of school.

In just the first quarter of this year alone, at least 75 of these mega-projects were blocked by residents who refuse to watch their electricity bills spike and their resources drain. So, the administration found a loophole for their billionaire donors: **stop asking local communities and just hand over federal public lands instead.** On Wednesday, the Department of Energy announced a massive $100 billion project to allow private corporations to build a sprawling AI server campus and a 2-gigawatt natural gas power plant directly on federal land in Kentucky. That is enough gas to power 750,000 homes, dedicated entirely to a corporate server farm. [**This is a five-alarm fire for our public lands, and we need to fight back immediately. name: Lieutenant Colonel Alex Vindman, US Army, Retired
subject: Not an easy decision
body:

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q32026?refcode=em260814-2&refcode2=1063_3892029_Uzh5q0&akid=1063%2E3892029%2EUzh5q0)
---
Alex Vindman here. With one day left until my August mid-month deadline expires, I am humbly asking you to make a donation to my U.S. Senate campaign in Florida.
I hope you will give me a chance to explain — but if you already know the importance of winning in Florida, then you can click here:
[**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q32026**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q32026?refcode=em260814-2&refcode2=1063_3892029_Uzh5q0&akid=1063%2E3892029%2EUzh5q0)
**Here is the truth: Running for the United States Senate was not an easy decision.** I knew the challenges going into this.
Ever since I blew the whistle on Donald Trump’s phone call with Ukraine, the president has had a vendetta against me. He attacks me every chance he gets on social media, and his billionaire allies will spend whatever it takes to pummel us in attack ads.
But as a former combat veteran in the United States Army, we don’t back down from a tough fight. We run towards it.
Our country is in chaos, and my opponent can’t seem to put public service before her own self-interest. Ashley Moody screwed Florida homeowners by caving to the big insurance companies, supported this administration that gutted disaster help for communities trying to rebuild, and traded more than $2 million in corporate stock last year while she had access to insider information only Congress gets.
Ashley Moody was hand-picked to be a ‘yes’ vote for Trump and the billionaire class. She is not Florida’s senator. She’s theirs.
So, that’s why I am running for the United States Senate. Because it’s time for us to make our voices heard and bring real leadership to Washington. **I know we can put Florida in play and save our democracy against an out-of-control president, but I cannot do it alone.**

Peter, thank you to everyone who supported my Annual Napa Summer Dinner at the beautiful Inglenook Winery!

I was honored to be surrounded by over 1,000 wonderful friends and several special guests. It was an honor to have Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi, Governor Tim Walz, former Governor Martin O'Malley, Congressman Adam Gray, and Assembly Majority Leader Cecilia Aguilar-Curry join us for the festivities.

I’m deeply grateful to have the support of our community and will keep fighting to protect our democracy, end forever wars, and lower costs for all. It was a wonderful night with delicious food from the Pasta King and world class wines from Napa Valley wineries.

Again, thank you for the special evening and I hope to see you again soon.

— Mike

| | **_Meet Rob:_** Born and raised in Kingston, PA, Rob Bresnahan is currently serving his first term as PA-08’s homegrown Congressman. He’s a fifth-generation Northeastern Pennsylvanian, and the only representative in Congress who is part of the National Electrical Contractors Association. A product of the American Dream, Rob learned the true meaning of hard work by getting his hands dirty early and often. He wired junction boxes, ran heavy equipment, drove trucks, and learned the value of an honest day’s work in the process. His family instilled the values of hard work, discipline, and perseverance in him at a young age – and Rob has stayed true to these foundational values all his life. At just 19 years old, Rob joined his family’s business as the CFO for Kuharchik Construction. He became the CEO of the company in 2013. Rob spent over a decade working and connecting with blue-collar Americans across the country before running for Congress in 2024. He was outspent 2:1 in his race against a 12-year Democrat that year, but the people of Northeastern Pennsylvania demanded change when they sent Rob to be their fighter in Washington. Through his experience as an electrical contractor, Rob saw the real world struggles facing America’s blue-collar workers first hand. Wages are not keeping up with the skyrocketing cost of living, and Americans who wake up every day and pay their dues are being left out to dry by their elected officials. But Rob’s voting record in Congress tells a different story. He’s stood up for hardworking Americans at every opportunity, regardless of partisan politics. Simply put, Rob Bresnahan brings both insight and candid concern for blue-collar America to Congress that your run-of-the-mill representatives don’t. Every day that he steps foot on Capitol Hill, Rob is 100% devoted to restoring America’s energy independence, deregulating the economy, and bringing well-paying jobs back to the great commonwealth of Pennsylvania. While he’s still serving his freshman term in Congress, Rob has already introduced key legislation to re-invest in American trades and pave avenues to success for young people who forgo a traditional college education. Now running for re-election in one of the most pivotal battleground races in the country, Rob is stepping up to the plate once again to deliver for the people of PA-08 and preserve our Republican House majority for the remainder of President Trump’s second term.

At the GOP Senate debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he’s
running to send me back to “bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken
restaurant.” He meant it as an insult.

As if the people who work in restaurants — cooking your food, clearing
your plates, keeping family businesses alive — have something to be
embarrassed about.

My great-grandfather came to New Hampshire from Greece over a century ago
and opened a candy shop in Manchester. My family built it into a
restaurant that’s been serving our community ever since.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260814_3.fPtkZS&refcode=em20260814-3&t=1003&akid=8321%2E582294%2EV2ku5Q ]Puritan Backroom sign

John Sununu was born into a political dynasty. His father was governor and
White House Chief of Staff. His brother was governor. John went to
Washington and then spent the next 17 years cashing in with Big Oil, Big
Pharma, and Wall Street.

Oh, and his family business invested in a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
that sells minerals to China. He’s never had to work hard a day in his
life — and his comments at that debate prove exactly what he thinks of
people who do.

The people who bus tables, flip burgers, and run small businesses in New
Hampshire don’t need a senator who looks down on them. They need one who
comes from them.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260814_3.fPtkZS&amount=5&refcode=em20260814-3&t=1022&akid=8321%2E582294%2EV2ku5Q ]Donate $5 »

John Sununu doesn’t know the real New Hampshire. I do. That’s why I’m
running for Senate.

— Chris Pappas

Peter, these two numbers keep me grounded: 1% and 0.3%.

1% is our primary margin of victory. 0.3% is Senator Elissa Slotkin’s
margin of victory when she beat the same opponent, Mike Rogers, in 2024.

No matter what the polls or betting markets say, we have to keep the same
mentality — one where we campaign like we're 10 points down.

That’s because just like in the primary, we’re up against tens of millions
of dollars that we’ll never match. We can’t get comfortable even for a
second — but we also don’t need to be scared.

We know what beats that kind of money: organizing.

That's why we’re hosting events, distributing campaign literature, and
talking to voters across Michigan. Spreading the word early and making
sure folks hear from us often is the only way we’ll win in November.

But none of that is free.

Reaching enough voters to overcome a multi-million-dollar campaign to stop
us costs more than what we have sitting in the bank right now.

That’s where I’m leaning on members of this grassroots team for support,
including you,
Peter.
